sources.title: J. Figueroa-O'Farrill, Brief Notes on the Calculus of Variations (University of Edinburgh, undergraduate lecture notes)

contents.name: Section 4, Theorem 1: Fundamental Lemma of the Calculus of Variations (one-variable statement; proof by contradiction with a bump supported where f > c > 0 and f h > c h)
contents.support: The recorded scalar proof follows exactly this contradiction pattern: a point where g > 0, a ball on which g >= g(p)/2, a nonnegative bump supported in that ball, and the positivity of the resulting pairing. The pair replaces the source's explicit bump construction with the published cutoff lemma lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization and closes the positivity step through the localization lemma and the order rules for the nonnegative integral.

contents.name: Section 4, construction of the smooth bump phi_{a,b}(t) = theta((t-a)/(b-a)) theta((b-t)/(b-a)) with theta(t) = e^{-1/t}, its positivity, and Remark 1 that it suffices to test smooth h
contents.support: Confirms that the test family in the pair's hypothesis can be taken smooth (C_c^infinity) and that the bump construction yields properties (P1) and (P2), the integral positivity pattern the recorded proof consumes.

contents.name: Section 14, Theorem 4: multidimensional version of the Fundamental Lemma (continuous f on a bounded open D, C^2 test functions vanishing on the boundary, product-of-bumps inside a hypercube) and Exercise 19
contents.support: Supplies the multidimensional bump construction inside a ball on which f > c; the pair states the compactly supported C_c^infinity(U) form, which the constructed bump's compact support gives. The pair generalises the pairing to vector-valued g componentwise.

contents.name: Section 14, classical fields: variation of the functional I[phi] = integral of L, the boundary flux integral over dR, the two admissible variation choices (fast decay or compact support), and the Euler-Lagrange equation (9) via the Fundamental Lemma, with the remark that the h of Theorem 4 has compact support
contents.support: Structural template for the recorded proof: expand the functional in the variation parameter, remove the boundary term under an explicitly stated compact-support hypothesis, and read off the coefficient equation using the fundamental variation lemma. The pair's item instantiates this for the kappa-scaled quadratic functional -F_{mu nu}F^{mu nu}/(4 kappa) + J^nu A_nu on a bounded open subset of R^4 with the (-,+,+,+) Minkowski conventions of def-em-minkowski-affine-space, and records the compact-support test identity explicitly instead of discarding a total derivative.

contents.name: Section 14, closing remark that the compact-support choice is licensed by Theorem 4's construction; Noether's theorem for actions defined by improper integrals
contents.reason: The compact-support remark is used only as confirmation of the route already recorded in the pair's own item; the Noether material is explicitly excluded by the design and M17 and is consumed by no page of this run, so it is recorded here and not built.

contents.name: Section 8, "Second variation" (printed pp. 10-11): at a stationary point an indefinite Hessian gives neither a maximum nor a minimum
contents.support: Source of the finite-dimensional saddle model of part (i) of the B example: the polynomial S(x,y)=x^2-y^2 has vanishing differential at the origin and S(epsilon,0)>0>S(0,epsilon), instantiating the source's statement that an indefinite Hessian yields neither extremum. The example's computation is self-contained; the citation records the source of the model, and the Step 3a finding refreshed this row from the earlier blanket out-of-scope disposition of Sections 5-12.

contents.name: Section 5.5.3, equation (5.42): S[A_mu] = -(1/(4 mu_0 c)) integral d^4x F_{mu nu}F^{mu nu}; Lorentz invariance of integrand and measure; expansion into (epsilon_0 E^2/2 - B^2/(2 mu_0))
contents.support: The quadratic field functional whose variation the pair computes. The pair keeps a general positive kappa and the design's (-,+,+,+) form eta of def-em-minkowski-affine-space, so it reuses the functional's structure and the fact that the density is a quadratic form in the first derivatives of A, not Tong's numerical normalisation or his (+,-,-,-) signature.

contents.name: Section 5.5.3, variation display: delta S = -(1/(mu_0 c)) integral F^{mu nu} partial_mu delta A_nu = (1/(mu_0 c)) integral (partial_mu F^{mu nu}) delta A_nu, 'discarding the total derivative term after integrating by parts', with delta S = 0 giving partial_mu F^{mu nu} = 0
contents.support: The exact expansion-antisymmetry-integration-by-parts route and the coefficient equation. The pair makes the discarded total derivative explicit: the first variation is converted with the weak-derivative test identity for the C^1 coefficients, which is legitimate precisely because the variation is compactly supported in U; the B example exhibits a non-compactly-supported variation for which that conversion fails.

contents.name: Section 5.5.3, equation (5.43) and the gauge-shift paragraph: source coupling S = (1/c) integral (-F^2/(4 mu_0) - A_mu J^mu), giving partial_mu F^{mu nu} = mu_0 J^nu; S -> S - (1/c) integral chi partial_mu J^mu under A_mu -> A_mu + partial_mu chi
contents.reason: The source-term sign dictionary (Tong couples with -A_mu J^mu and concludes partial_mu F^{mu nu} = +mu_0 J^nu, while the pair's density carries +J^nu A_nu and concludes partial_mu F^{mu nu} = -kappa J^nu) is recorded in this row and in the pair's notes; the gauge-variation computation and current conservation are the content of the physics theorem pthm-em-action-gauge-source-compatibility on em-action-and-variational-formulation, whose reservation completes them as V2.

note: Convention dictionary. Tong uses the (+,-,-,-) Minkowski metric and couples the source with -A_mu J^mu, obtaining partial_mu F^{mu nu} = mu_0 J^nu; this pair uses the (-,+,+,+) form eta of def-em-minkowski-affine-space and the density -F_{mu nu}F^{mu nu}/(4 kappa) + J^nu A_nu, obtaining partial_mu F^{mu nu} = -kappa J^nu. Only the computation's structure is reused, and every sign is rederived in the pair's conventions. Figueroa-O'Farrill's Theorem 4 states the multidimensional fundamental lemma for C^2 functions vanishing on the boundary of a bounded open set; the pair states the C_c^infinity(U) form, whose bump construction and compact support are the source's, with smoothness delegated to the published cutoff lemma. Particle-curve variation (V1) and gauge/source compatibility (V2) belong to em-expanded-analysis-prerequisites and em-action-and-variational-formulation respectively and are not built on this pair.
